properties.description: The main population of African countries is concentrated along the life expectancy axis in the intermediate range between approximately 60 and 68 years.
The distribution of country life expectancy shows a clear concentration of marks across the central-to-high life expectancy range (approximately 60 to 85 years).
Haiti departs significantly from the main Americas population distribution with an isolated low life expectancy.
Cape Verde exhibits the greatest life expectancy among all African countries in the scope, positioned furthest to the right along the horizontal axis.
Lesotho exhibits the least life expectancy among all African countries in the scope, positioned furthest to the left along the horizontal axis.
Lesotho (point_71) has the minimum life expectancy in the dataset, located at the leftmost position on the Life expectancy axis.
Singapore (point_1) has the maximum life expectancy in the dataset, located at the rightmost position on the Life expectancy axis.
Canada exhibits the maximum visible life expectancy among all countries within the Americas scope.
Haiti exhibits the minimum visible life expectancy among all countries within the Americas scope.
Singapore exhibits the maximum life expectancy among the observed Asian countries, situated furthest to the right along the horizontal axis.
Solomon Islands exhibits the minimum life expectancy among the observed Asian countries, situated furthest to the left along the horizontal axis.

Comparing regional maximum life expectancy values shows that Singapore in Asia reaches the highest maximum, positioned furthest to the right compared to the maximums of Canada in the Americas and Cape Verde in Africa.

Comparing regional minimum life expectancy values shows that Lesotho in Africa has the lowest minimum, positioned furthest to the left compared to the regional minimums of Solomon Islands in Asia and Haiti in the Americas.
